source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

method: Every pinned Greek verse read before authoring. All verses drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW is a post-authoring comparator, not a wording template. Each authored verse has its own rationale. F0–F3 choices are provisional; no independent review or change quota.

verses.rationale: Keeps both senders, slave status, the whole community and its named offices.
verses.before: Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, together with the overseers and deacons:
verses.after: From Paul and Timothy, slaves of Christ Jesus, to all the saints in Christ Jesus at Philippi, together with the overseers and deacons.
verses.tsw_comparator: Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, together with the overseers and deacons:

verses.rationale: Retains the compact blessing and its two named sources without gratuitous rewording.
verses.before: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.after: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.rationale: Makes the remembrance idiom natural; the alternative direction is noted.
verses.before: I thank my God every time I remember you,
verses.after: I thank my God whenever I remember you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I give thanks to my God every time I remember you,

verses.rationale: Keeps every/all/always emphasis and connects the reason in the following verse.
verses.before: always praying with joy in every prayer for all of you,
verses.after: In every prayer for all of you, I always pray with joy
verses.tsw_comparator: always, in every prayer of mine for all of you, making my prayer with joy,

verses.rationale: Preserves partnership as continuing participation rather than mere financial support.
verses.before: because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now.
verses.after: because of your partnership in the good news from the first day until now.
verses.tsw_comparator: because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine initiative, communal scope and the named future day.
verses.before: I am confident of this: the one who began a good work among you will bring it to completion by the day of Christ Jesus.
verses.after: I am sure of this: the one who began a good work among you will bring it to completion by the day of Christ Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I am confident of this: that the one who began a good work among you will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ.

verses.rationale: Splits the long sentence while preserving all, shared grace and both settings.
verses.before: It is right for me to think this way about all of you, because I hold you in my heart. All of you share grace with me, both in my imprisonment and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel.
verses.after: It is right for me to feel this way about all of you, because I hold you in my heart. All of you share in grace with me, both in my imprisonment and in defending and confirming the good news.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is right for me to think this way about all of you, because I hold you in my heart, for all of you share with me in grace, both in my imprisonment and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel.

verses.rationale: Expresses the bodily affection idiom without reducing the intensity or its Christ relation.
verses.before: God is my witness how deeply I long for all of you with the affection of Christ Jesus.
verses.after: God is my witness to how I long for all of you with the deep affection of Christ Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: For God is my witness, how I long for all of you with the affection of Christ Jesus.

verses.rationale: Keeps increasing love joined to knowledge and perception.
verses.before: And this is my prayer: that your love may abound more and more in knowledge and every kind of discernment,
verses.after: And this is my prayer: that your love may overflow more and more in knowledge and every kind of discernment,
verses.tsw_comparator: And this is my prayer: that your love may abound still more and more in knowledge and all discernment,

verses.rationale: Makes the purpose and discernment clear while retaining the future horizon.
verses.before: so that you may discern what truly matters and may be pure and blameless for the day of Christ,
verses.after: so that you can recognize what matters most and be sincere and blameless for the day of Christ,
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you may discern what truly matters, and so be pure and blameless for the day of Christ,

verses.rationale: Keeps the fruit image, mediated righteousness and divine glory.
verses.before: filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
verses.after: filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, to God's glory and praise.
verses.tsw_comparator: filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unexpected advance through adverse events and the inclusive community address.
verses.before: I want you to know, brothers and sisters, that what has happened to me has actually helped advance the gospel.
verses.after: I want you to know, brothers and sisters, that what has happened to me has actually advanced the good news.
verses.tsw_comparator: I want you to know, brothers and sisters, that what has happened to me has actually served to advance the gospel,

verses.rationale: Retains the imprisonment and its Christ-related cause; guard/place ambiguity is noted.
verses.before: As a result, it has become clear throughout the whole imperial guard and to everyone else that I am in chains for Christ,
verses.after: It has become clear throughout the whole imperial guard, and to everyone else, that I am in chains because of Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that it has become known throughout the whole imperial guard and to all the rest that my imprisonment is for Christ;

verses.rationale: Keeps most rather than many, the causal chains and increased boldness.
verses.before: and most of the brothers and sisters have become more confident in the Lord because of my imprisonment and are much more daring in speaking the word without fear.
verses.after: And most of the brothers and sisters, gaining confidence in the Lord through my chains, now dare more than ever to speak the word without fear.
verses.tsw_comparator: and most of the brothers and sisters, having become confident in the Lord through my imprisonment, dare all the more to speak the word without fear.

verses.rationale: Preserves opposed motives without changing the shared proclamation.
verses.before: Some proclaim Christ out of envy and rivalry, but others out of goodwill.
verses.after: Some indeed preach Christ out of envy and rivalry, while others do so out of goodwill.
verses.tsw_comparator: Some indeed proclaim Christ out of envy and rivalry, but others out of goodwill.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the latter referent while keeping appointed/placed language open.
verses.before: The latter do so out of love, knowing that I am here for the defense of the gospel.
verses.after: The latter act out of love, knowing that I am placed here to defend the good news.
verses.tsw_comparator: The latter do so out of love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the gospel.

verses.rationale: Retains the harmful intention and its relation to imprisonment.
verses.before: The former proclaim Christ out of selfish ambition, not sincerely, thinking they can add trouble to my imprisonment.
verses.after: The others proclaim Christ out of selfish ambition, without sincere motives, thinking they can add to my distress in prison.
verses.tsw_comparator: The former proclaim Christ out of selfish ambition, not sincerely, thinking to afflict me in my imprisonment.

verses.rationale: Preserves the rhetorical question and transition from present to future joy.
verses.before: What does it matter? Only this: in every way, whether from false motives or in truth, Christ is proclaimed—and in that I rejoice. Yes, and I will continue to rejoice,
verses.after: What does it matter? In every way, whether as a pretense or in truth, Christ is being proclaimed, and in this I rejoice. Yes, I will go on rejoicing,
verses.tsw_comparator: What then? Only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed—and in that I rejoice.

verses.rationale: Retains salvation rather than guaranteeing release from prison and keeps both means.
verses.before: because I know that this will turn out for my deliverance through your prayers and the help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ.
verses.after: because I know that through your prayers and the help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ, this will lead to my salvation.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I know that this will turn out for my deliverance through your prayers and the help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily witness and both possible outcomes without resolving the tension.
verses.before: My eager expectation and hope is that I will not be put to shame in anything, but that with complete boldness, now as always, Christ will be exalted in my body, whether through life or through death.
verses.after: My eager expectation and hope is that I will not be put to shame in any way, but that with complete boldness, now as always, Christ will be magnified in my body, whether by life or by death.
verses.tsw_comparator: according to my eager expectation and hope that I will not be put to shame in anything, but that with all boldness, now as always, Christ will be exalted in my body, whether by life or by death.

verses.rationale: Preserves the aphorism's terse parallelism.
verses.before: For to me, to live is Christ and to die is gain.
verses.after: For to me, living is Christ and dying is gain.
verses.tsw_comparator: For to me, to live is Christ and to die is gain.

verses.rationale: Makes the conditional understandable while retaining flesh and unresolved choice.
verses.before: If I continue living in the flesh, that means fruitful work for me. Yet I do not know which I would choose.
verses.after: But if I go on living in the flesh, that means fruitful work for me. Which I would choose, I do not know.
verses.tsw_comparator: If I am to live on in the flesh, that means fruitful labor for me; and I do not know which I should choose.

verses.rationale: Carries the pressure and comparative intensity without explaining the manner of departure.
verses.before: I am torn between the two. I desire to depart and be with Christ, which is far better,
verses.after: I am pulled in both directions. I long to depart and be with Christ, for that is far better;
verses.tsw_comparator: I am hard pressed between the two: my desire is to depart and be with Christ, for that is far better;

verses.rationale: Retains the community's need as the counterweight to personal desire.
verses.before: but to remain in the flesh is more necessary for your sake.
verses.after: yet remaining in the flesh is more necessary for your sake.
verses.tsw_comparator: but to remain in the flesh is more necessary for your sake.

verses.rationale: Keeps confidence, continued presence and the two purposes.
verses.before: Convinced of this, I know that I will remain and continue with all of you for your progress and joy in faith,
verses.after: Convinced of this, I know that I will remain and continue with all of you for your progress and joy in faith,
verses.tsw_comparator: Convinced of this, I know that I will remain and continue with all of you for your progress and joy in faith,

verses.rationale: Preserves boasting located in Christ and occasioned by Paul's return.
verses.before: so that your boasting in Christ Jesus may overflow because of me when I come to you again.
verses.after: so that your boasting in Christ Jesus may overflow because of me when I am with you again.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that in me you may have ample cause to boast in Christ Jesus because of my coming to you again.

verses.rationale: Retains civic language, common struggle and spirit/soul imagery without deciding the spirit's referent.
verses.before: Only live as citizens in a way worthy of the gospel of Christ, so that whether I come and see you or remain absent, I may hear that you are standing firm in one spirit, striving together with one mind for the faith of the gospel,
verses.after: Only, live as citizens worthy of the good news of Christ. Then, whether I come and see you or remain absent, I may hear that you stand firm in one spirit, struggling together with one soul for the faith of the good news,
verses.tsw_comparator: Only live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ, so that whether I come and see you or am absent and hear about you, I may know that you are standing firm in one spirit, striving side by side with one mind for the faith of the gospel,

verses.rationale: Keeps opposed outcomes and divine origin without specifying the opponents.
verses.before: without being intimidated in any way by your opponents. This is a sign to them of destruction, but to you of salvation—and this is from God.
verses.after: unafraid of your opponents in any way. This is a sign to them of destruction, but of your salvation—and this comes from God.
verses.tsw_comparator: and not intimidated in any way by your opponents. This is a sign of their destruction, but of your salvation—and this is from God.

verses.rationale: Makes the gracious-gift construction audible without making all suffering the same kind.
verses.before: For you have been graciously given, on behalf of Christ, not only to trust in him but also to suffer for him,
verses.after: For you have been given the privilege, for Christ's sake, not only of believing in him but also of suffering for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he has graciously granted you the privilege not only of trusting in Christ, but also of suffering for him,

verses.rationale: Preserves the shared struggle across past sight and present report.
verses.before: since you are engaged in the same struggle you saw me have and now hear that I still have.
verses.after: You are engaged in the same struggle that you saw in me and now hear that I still face.
verses.tsw_comparator: since you are having the same struggle that you saw I had and now hear that I still have.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated conditional appeal and four relational grounds.
verses.before: So if there is any encouragement in Christ, any comfort from love, any sharing in the Spirit, any affection and compassion,
verses.after: So if there is any encouragement in Christ, any comfort from love, any sharing in the Spirit, any tenderness and compassion,
verses.tsw_comparator: If then there is any encouragement in Christ, any consolation from love, any sharing in the Spirit, any compassion and mercy,

verses.rationale: Makes the appeal natural while retaining love, soul and repeated common-mindedness.
verses.before: make my joy complete by being of the same mind, having the same love, united in spirit, thinking as one.
verses.after: make my joy complete: think in harmony, share the same love, be united in soul and of one mind.
verses.tsw_comparator: make my joy complete: be of the same mind, having the same love, being in full accord and of one mind.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sharp contrast and comparative valuation of others.
verses.before: Do nothing from selfish ambition or empty conceit, but in humility consider others as more important than yourselves.
verses.after: Do nothing out of selfish ambition or empty pride. Instead, in humility regard others as more important than yourselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility regard others as better than yourselves.

verses.rationale: Keeps the also of the source rather than denying all concern for one's own needs.
verses.before: Let each of you look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others.
verses.after: Each of you should look beyond your own interests to the interests of others as well.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let each of you look not to your own interests, but to the interests of others.

verses.rationale: Keeps the communal mindset and connection with Christ; alternative relation is noted.
verses.before: Have this mindset among yourselves, which is also yours in Christ Jesus:
verses.after: Let this be your way of thinking together, the way of Christ Jesus:
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the same mind be in you that was in Christ Jesus,

verses.rationale: Retains form and equality while selecting exploitation with the alternative noted.
verses.before: who, existing in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as something to be exploited,
verses.after: Though he was in the form of God, he did not regard equality with God as something to exploit.
verses.tsw_comparator: who, though he was in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as something to be exploited,

verses.rationale: Keeps emptying unexplained and connects it to slave form and human likeness.
verses.before: but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, becoming like human beings. And being found in human form,
verses.after: Instead, he emptied himself, taking the form of a slave, becoming like human beings. And being found in human form,
verses.tsw_comparator: but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being born in human likeness.

verses.rationale: Preserves the downward movement and climactic specification of crucifixion.
verses.before: he humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death— even death on a cross.
verses.after: he humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death— even death on a cross.
verses.tsw_comparator: And being found in human form, he humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death—even death on a cross.

verses.rationale: Keeps the divine action as response and the unequaled name unnamed here.
verses.before: Therefore God highly exalted him and graciously gave him the name that is above every name,
verses.after: That is why God raised him to the highest place and gave him the name above every name,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore God highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name,

verses.rationale: Retains the threefold cosmic range rather than compressing it to everyone.
verses.before: so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend— in heaven, on earth, and under the earth—
verses.after: so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend— in heaven, on earth and beneath the earth—
verses.tsw_comparator: so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend, in heaven and on earth and under the earth,

verses.rationale: Preserves confession, the Lord title and its stated divine purpose.
verses.before: and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
verses.after: and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
verses.tsw_comparator: and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

verses.rationale: Keeps the plural community's work, fear and trembling, and the presence/absence contrast.
verses.before: Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed—not only when I was present, but now much more in my absence—work out your own salvation with fear and trembling,
verses.after: So then, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling—not only when I am present, but much more now while I am absent.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling;

verses.rationale: Makes the two divine workings audible while keeping communal/inward scope open in the note.
verses.before: for God is the one working in you, both to desire and to work for his good pleasure.
verses.after: For God is at work in you—in your willing as well as your doing—for his good pleasure.
verses.tsw_comparator: for it is God who is at work in you, enabling you both to will and to work for his good pleasure.

verses.rationale: Preserves the comprehensive instruction and both kinds of discord.
verses.before: Do everything without grumbling and arguing,
verses.after: Do everything without grumbling or arguing,
verses.tsw_comparator: Do all things without murmuring and arguing,

verses.rationale: Keeps the purpose, child identity and light image within the difficult generational language.
verses.before: so that you may be blameless and innocent, children of God without blemish in the midst of a crooked and twisted generation, among whom you shine like lights in the world,
verses.after: so that you may be blameless and innocent, God's children without blemish in the midst of a crooked and distorted generation. Among them you shine like lights in the world,
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you may be blameless and innocent, children of God without blemish in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom you shine like lights in the world,

verses.rationale: Retains holding/word and the repeated in-vain clauses with an alternative note.
verses.before: holding firmly to the word of life, so that on the day of Christ I may boast that I did not run in vain or labor in vain.
verses.after: holding firmly to the word of life. Then I can boast on the day of Christ that I did not run in vain or labor in vain.
verses.tsw_comparator: holding fast to the word of life, so that on the day of Christ I may boast that I did not run in vain or labor in vain.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sacrificial image and communal faith without defining the pouring out as completed death.
verses.before: But even if I am being poured out as a drink offering over the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and rejoice together with all of you.
verses.after: But even if I am being poured out as a drink offering over the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and share my joy with all of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But even if I am being poured out as a libation upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and rejoice with all of you;

verses.rationale: Preserves the reciprocal rejoicing.
verses.before: In the same way, you also should rejoice and rejoice together with me.
verses.after: You too should rejoice in the same way and share your joy with me.
verses.tsw_comparator: and in the same way you also should rejoice and rejoice with me.

verses.rationale: Retains hope qualified in the Lord and the desired return of news.
verses.before: I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I too may be encouraged when I hear how you are doing.
verses.after: I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I too may be encouraged when I learn how you are.
verses.tsw_comparator: I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I too may be encouraged by news of you.

verses.rationale: Conveys like-souled concern without turning the comparison into a universal judgment.
verses.before: I have no one else like him who will genuinely care about your welfare,
verses.after: I have no one else of his spirit who will take a sincere interest in your welfare.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I have no one like him, who will be genuinely concerned for your welfare.

verses.rationale: Retains the source's forceful contrast without inserting exceptions.
verses.before: because everyone else seeks their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
verses.after: For all the others seek their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: All of them seek their own interests, not the interests of Jesus Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps proven service, familial comparison and the slave verb without making Paul his master.
verses.before: But you know Timothy's proven character, how, like a child with a parent, he has served with me in the work of the gospel.
verses.after: But you know Timothy's proven character. Like a child with a father, he has served with me as a slave for the good news.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you know Timothy’s proven worth, how like a child serving a parent he has served with me in the work of the gospel.

verses.rationale: Preserves the conditional timing rather than promising a definite date.
verses.before: So I hope to send him as soon as I see how things go with me,
verses.after: So I hope to send him as soon as I see how things turn out for me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I hope therefore to send him just as soon as I see how things go with me;

verses.rationale: Retains the personal visit and its confidence in the Lord.
verses.before: and I trust in the Lord that I myself will also come soon.
verses.after: And I am confident in the Lord that I myself will come soon.
verses.tsw_comparator: and I trust in the Lord that I myself will come soon.

verses.rationale: Keeps all five roles and their distinct relational directions.
verses.before: I considered it necessary to send Epaphroditus back to you—my brother, coworker, and fellow soldier, and your messenger and minister to my need.
verses.after: Still, I thought it necessary to send you Epaphroditus—my brother, fellow worker and fellow soldier, and your messenger and minister to my needs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Still, I think it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus—my brother and coworker and fellow soldier, your messenger and minister to my need—

verses.rationale: Preserves his concern over their hearing, not only over illness itself.
verses.before: He has been longing for all of you and has been distressed because you heard that he was ill.
verses.after: He has been longing for all of you and was distressed because you heard that he was ill.
verses.tsw_comparator: for he has been longing for all of you and has been distressed because you heard that he was ill.

verses.rationale: Keeps near death, mercy to both people and accumulating grief.
verses.before: He was indeed ill and nearly died. But God had mercy on him, and not only on him but also on me, so that I would not have sorrow upon sorrow.
verses.after: Indeed, he was ill and nearly died. But God had mercy on him, and not only on him but also on me, sparing me sorrow upon sorrow.
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed he was ill, and near to death. But God had mercy on him, and not only on him but also on me, so that I would not have sorrow upon sorrow.

verses.rationale: Makes the epistolary sending natural while retaining both emotional results.
verses.before: So I am all the more eager to send him, so that when you see him again you may rejoice and I may be less anxious.
verses.after: So I am all the more eager to send him, so that seeing him again may bring you joy and lessen my sorrow.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am all the more eager to send him, therefore, so that you may rejoice at seeing him again, and that I may be less anxious.

verses.rationale: Preserves the command's extension beyond the one messenger.
verses.before: Welcome him in the Lord with all joy, and honor people like him,
verses.after: Welcome him in the Lord with all joy, and hold people like him in honor,
verses.tsw_comparator: Welcome him then in the Lord with all joy, and honor such people,

verses.rationale: Keeps risk, Christ's work and the practical lack without alleging their unwillingness.
verses.before: because he came close to death for the work of Christ, risking his life to complete what was lacking in your service to me.
verses.after: because he came close to death for Christ's work, risking his life to provide the service you could not give me.
verses.tsw_comparator: because he came close to death for the work of Christ, risking his life to complete what was lacking in your service to me.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated instruction as protective and the familial address.
verses.before: Finally, my brothers and sisters, rejoice in the Lord. It is no trouble for me to write the same things to you, and for you it is a safeguard.
verses.after: Finally, my brothers and sisters, rejoice in the Lord. Writing the same things to you is no burden to me, and it is a safeguard for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Finally, my brothers and sisters, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you is not troublesome to me, and for you it is safe.

verses.rationale: Preserves the triple warning, harsh animal image and circumcision wordplay in a note.
verses.before: Watch out for the dogs. Watch out for the evil workers. Watch out for those who mutilate the flesh.
verses.after: Watch out for the dogs! Watch out for the evil workers! Watch out for those who mutilate the flesh!
verses.tsw_comparator: Beware of the dogs, beware of the evil workers, beware of those who mutilate the flesh.

verses.rationale: Keeps the community claim and the three defining participles.
verses.before: For we are the circumcision—we who worship by the Spirit of God, boast in Christ Jesus, and put no confidence in the flesh,
verses.after: For we are the circumcision: we worship by God's Spirit, boast in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh,
verses.tsw_comparator: For we are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God and boast in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh—

verses.rationale: Retains the flesh refrain and the comparative challenge.
verses.before: though I myself have reasons for confidence even in the flesh. If anyone else thinks they have reasons for confidence in the flesh, I have more:
verses.after: though I too have grounds for confidence in the flesh. If anyone else thinks they have such grounds, I have more:
verses.tsw_comparator: though I myself have reason for confidence in the flesh. If anyone else thinks he has reason for confidence in the flesh, I have more:

verses.rationale: Preserves every biographical marker and the eighth day.
verses.before: circumcised on the eighth day, from the people of Israel, from the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee;
verses.after: circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew born of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee;
verses.tsw_comparator: circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew born of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee;

verses.rationale: Keeps persecution explicit alongside the claim of legal blamelessness.
verses.before: as to zeal, a persecutor of the church; as to righteousness under the law, blameless.
verses.after: as to zeal, a persecutor of the church; as to righteousness under the law, blameless.
verses.tsw_comparator: as to zeal, a persecutor of the church; as to righteousness under the law, blameless.

verses.rationale: Retains the accounting reversal and plural gains to singular loss.
verses.before: But whatever gains I had, I have come to regard these as loss because of Christ.
verses.after: But whatever counted as gains for me, I have counted as loss because of Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: But whatever gains I had, these I have come to regard as loss because of Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps the intensifying everything and the offensive discard image with its range in a note.
verses.before: More than that, I regard everything as loss because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. Because of him I have lost all things, and I regard them as rubbish, so that I may gain Christ
verses.after: More than that, I count everything as loss compared with the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For him I have lost everything, and I count it as refuse so that I may gain Christ
verses.tsw_comparator: More than that, I regard everything as loss because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For his sake I have suffered the loss of all things, and I regard them as rubbish,

verses.rationale: Preserves both faith expressions and records the consequential alternative faith in Christ.
verses.before: and be found in him—not having my own righteousness from the law, but the righteousness that comes through the faithfulness of Christ, the righteousness from God grounded in trust.
verses.after: and be found in him, having no righteousness of my own from the law, but the righteousness that comes through Christ's faithfulness, the righteousness from God on the basis of faith.
verses.tsw_comparator: and be found in him—not with a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but one that comes through trust in Christ, a righteousness from God grounded in trust.

verses.rationale: Retains knowing, power, participation and conformity without making suffering disappear.
verses.before: I want to know him—the power of his resurrection and the sharing of his sufferings—becoming conformed to his death,
verses.after: I want to know him, the power of his resurrection and the sharing of his sufferings, being shaped into the likeness of his death,
verses.tsw_comparator: I want to know Christ—and the power of his resurrection—and the sharing of his sufferings, becoming like him in his death,

verses.rationale: Keeps the source's tentative reaching rather than supplying certainty.
verses.before: if somehow I may attain the resurrection from the dead.
verses.after: if somehow I may reach the resurrection from the dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: if somehow I may attain the resurrection from the dead.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated grasping language and the incomplete attainment.
verses.before: Not that I have already received this or have already been made complete, but I press on to take hold of it because Christ Jesus has taken hold of me.
verses.after: Not that I have already obtained this or have already been made perfect. But I press on to take hold of it, because Christ has taken hold of me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Not that I have already taken hold of this or have already been made complete, but I press on to make it my own, because Christ Jesus has made me his own.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated denial and bodily reaching image.
verses.before: Brothers and sisters, I do not consider myself to have taken hold of it. But one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and reaching forward to what lies ahead,
verses.after: Brothers and sisters, I do not consider that I have taken hold of it. But one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and stretching toward what lies ahead,
verses.tsw_comparator: Brothers and sisters, I do not consider that I have made it my own; but one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead,

verses.rationale: Preserves goal, prize and upward call without explaining the prize beyond the text.
verses.before: I press on toward the goal for the prize of God's upward call in Christ Jesus.
verses.after: I press on toward the goal, for the prize of God's upward call in Christ Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: I press on toward the goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus.

verses.rationale: Keeps the mature/perfect word connection and room for differing thought.
verses.before: So let those of us who are mature think this way. And if you think differently about anything, God will reveal that to you as well.
verses.after: Let all of us who are mature think this way. And if you think differently about anything, God will reveal that to you too.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let those of us who are mature think this way; and if in anything you think differently, God will make this clear to you also.

verses.rationale: Follows the short pinned reading without adding the longer rule or mindset clauses.
verses.before: Only let us keep living in line with what we have already attained.
verses.after: Only, let us keep in step with what we have already attained.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only let us hold fast to what we have already attained.

verses.rationale: Keeps the shift from my to us and the community's attention to examples.
verses.before: Brothers and sisters, join together in imitating me, and pay attention to those who live according to the pattern you have in us.
verses.after: Join in following my example, brothers and sisters, and pay attention to those who live by the pattern you have in us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Brothers and sisters, join in imitating me, and pay close attention to those who live according to the pattern you have in us.

verses.rationale: Retains the accusation as the speaker's grief-laden statement.
verses.before: For many live as enemies of the cross of Christ. I have often told you about them, and now I tell you even with tears.
verses.after: For many live as enemies of Christ's cross. I have often told you about them, and now I tell you even with tears.
verses.tsw_comparator: For many live as enemies of the cross of Christ; I have often told you of them, and now I tell you even with tears.

verses.rationale: Keeps all four claims and the bodily belly metaphor.
verses.before: Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and their glory is in their shame. Their minds are set on earthly things.
verses.after: Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and their glory is in their shame. Their minds are set on earthly things.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their end is destruction; their god is the belly; their glory is in their shame; their minds are set on earthly things.

verses.rationale: Preserves civic identity, waiting and the full title without adding escape imagery.
verses.before: But our citizenship is in heaven, and from there we eagerly await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.after: But our citizenship is in heaven, and from there we eagerly await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: But our citizenship is in heaven, and from there we await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily transformation and its relation to universal subjection.
verses.before: He will transform our humiliated body to be conformed to his glorious body, by the power that enables him even to bring all things under his rule.
verses.after: He will transform our lowly body to be like his glorious body, by the power that enables him to bring all things under his rule.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will transform the body of our humiliation so that it may be conformed to the body of his glory, by the power that enables him to bring all things under his rule.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated affection, longing and the crown image.
verses.before: Therefore, my brothers and sisters, whom I love and long for, my joy and crown, stand firm in the Lord in this way, my beloved.
verses.after: So, my beloved brothers and sisters whom I long for, my joy and crown, stand firm in the Lord in this way, my beloved.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, my brothers and sisters, whom I love and long for, my joy and crown, stand firm in this way in the Lord, my beloved.

verses.rationale: Keeps equal repeated appeals to both named women.
verses.before: I urge Euodia, and I urge Syntyche, to have the same mind in the Lord.
verses.after: I appeal to Euodia, and I appeal to Syntyche: be of one mind in the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: I urge Euodia and I urge Syntyche to be of the same mind in the Lord.

verses.rationale: Retains the women's active labor, named colleague and the book image without inventing the companion's identity.
verses.before: Yes, and I ask you also, my true companion, help these women. They struggled alongside me in the gospel, together with Clement and the rest of my coworkers, whose names are in the book of life.
verses.after: Yes, I ask you too, my true companion, help these women. They struggled beside me for the good news, along with Clement and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are in the book of life.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yes, and I ask you also, my true companion, help these women, for they struggled beside me in the work of the gospel, together with Clement and the rest of my coworkers, whose names are in the book of life.

verses.rationale: Retains the deliberately repeated imperative.
verses.before: Rejoice in the Lord always. Again I will say: rejoice.
verses.after: Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: rejoice!
verses.tsw_comparator: Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, Rejoice.

verses.rationale: Keeps universal visibility and the open spatial/temporal nearness.
verses.before: Let your gentleness be known to everyone. The Lord is near.
verses.after: Let everyone know your gentleness. The Lord is near.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let your gentleness be known to everyone. The Lord is near.

verses.rationale: Preserves anything/everything and all three modes of address without adding diagnosis or advice.
verses.before: Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
verses.after: Do not be anxious about anything. Instead, in everything, with prayer, petition and thanksgiving, make your requests known to God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not worry about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.

verses.rationale: Keeps incomprehensible peace and the guarding image over both hearts and minds.
verses.before: And the peace of God, which surpasses every understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.
verses.after: And God's peace, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.

verses.rationale: Retains all six qualities and both conditional values in readable sequence.
verses.before: Finally, brothers and sisters, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is pleasing, whatever is commendable—if there is any excellence and if there is anything worthy of praise—think about these things.
verses.after: Finally, brothers and sisters, whatever is true, honorable, just, pure, lovely or commendable—if anything is excellent, if anything deserves praise—give these things your attention.
verses.tsw_comparator: Finally, brothers and sisters, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is pleasing, whatever is commendable—if there is any excellence and if there is anything worthy of praise—think about these things.

verses.rationale: Preserves all four forms of reception and the God-of-peace promise.
verses.before: Keep practicing what you learned and received and heard and saw in me, and the God of peace will be with you.
verses.after: Put into practice what you learned and received and heard and saw in me, and the God of peace will be with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Keep on doing the things that you have learned and received and heard and seen in me, and the God of peace will be with you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the flourishing image and explicitly avoids blaming them for the interruption.
verses.before: I rejoiced greatly in the Lord that now at last your concern for me has flourished again. You were indeed concerned for me, but you had no opportunity.
verses.after: I rejoiced greatly in the Lord that your concern for me has blossomed again. You were concerned before, but had no opportunity to act.
verses.tsw_comparator: I rejoiced in the Lord greatly that now at last you have revived your concern for me; indeed, you were concerned for me, but you had no opportunity.

verses.rationale: Retains learned contentment and the speaker's qualification of his thanks.
verses.before: I do not say this because I am in need, for I have learned to be content in whatever circumstances I am.
verses.after: I am not saying this because I am in need, for I have learned to be content in whatever circumstances I face.
verses.tsw_comparator: Not that I am speaking of being in need, for I have learned to be content with whatever I have.

verses.rationale: Keeps the paired bodily and economic conditions rather than a generalized success claim.
verses.before: I know how to be brought low, and I know how to abound. In any and every circumstance I have learned the secret—being well fed and being hungry, having abundance and being in need.
verses.after: I know how to live with little, and I know how to have plenty. In every situation I have learned the secret: being well fed or hungry, having plenty or going without.
verses.tsw_comparator: I know what it is to be brought low, and I know what it is to abound. In any and every circumstance, I have learned the secret of facing plenty and hunger, abundance and need.

verses.rationale: Retains the broad all things expression and the unnamed strengthening agent; immediate circumstances remain in a note.
verses.before: I can do all things through the one who strengthens me.
verses.after: I have strength for all things through the one who strengthens me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I can do all things through the one who strengthens me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the corrective still and their participation in hardship.
verses.before: Still, you did well to share in my trouble.
verses.after: Still, you did well to share in my distress.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet it was kind of you to share in my trouble.

verses.rationale: Retains place, time, unique partnership and the accounting metaphor.
verses.before: And you Philippians know that in the beginning of the gospel, when I left Macedonia, no church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving except you alone.
verses.after: You Philippians know that in the early days of the good news, when I left Macedonia, no church shared with me in the account of giving and receiving except you alone.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you Philippians yourselves know that in the beginning of the gospel, when I left Macedonia, no church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving except you alone.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named location and the idiomatic repeated provision.
verses.before: Even when I was in Thessalonica, you sent help for my needs more than once.
verses.after: Even in Thessalonica, you sent help for my needs more than once.
verses.tsw_comparator: For even in Thessalonica you sent me help for my needs more than once.

verses.rationale: Preserves fruit and account imagery together rather than reducing it to money.
verses.before: Not that I seek the gift itself; I seek the fruit that increases to your account.
verses.after: It is not the gift I seek, but the fruit that grows to your account.
verses.tsw_comparator: Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the fruit that increases to your account.

verses.rationale: Retains receipt language, the messenger and all sacrificial descriptions.
verses.before: I have received everything in full and have more than enough. I am well supplied, having received from Epaphroditus the gifts you sent—a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.
verses.after: I have received everything in full and have more than enough. I am well supplied now that I have received your gifts from Epaphroditus—a fragrant aroma, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have received full payment and more; I am well supplied, having received from Epaphroditus the gifts you sent, a fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God.

verses.rationale: Keeps every need, God's measure of supply and the relation to Christ.
verses.before: And my God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
verses.after: And my God will meet every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: And my God will fully supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.

verses.rationale: Preserves the doxology's single addressee and unending scope.
verses.before: To our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.after: To our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.tsw_comparator: To our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.

verses.rationale: Keeps each recipient and the distinct nearby sending group.
verses.before: Greet every saint in Christ Jesus. The brothers and sisters who are with me greet you.
verses.after: Greet every saint in Christ Jesus. The brothers and sisters with me send you greetings.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet every saint in Christ Jesus. The brothers and sisters who are with me greet you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the whole group and the specified imperial household without identifying occupations.
verses.before: All the saints greet you, especially those of Caesar's household.
verses.after: All the saints send you greetings, especially those of Caesar's household.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the saints greet you, especially those of the emperor’s household.

verses.rationale: Retains the singular spirit addressed to the plural community and the short ending.
verses.before: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
verses.after: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
